clauses.reason: Record the approved workspace outcomes and the abandonment authorization before implementation.

updates.rationale: Ancestry alone misses work that reached the delivery branch through a cherry-pick or another batch, so those worktrees waited for the owner. Patch identity is what Git itself uses to recognize an applied commit, and the dense combined diff exposes a merge resolution that would otherwise hide content outside every commit. The tree comparison covers squashed or re-resolved landings without trusting history shape; it is conservative when the delivery branch later changed the same path. Fresh workspaces stay because an Agent may have just opened one. Ready receipts are not consulted because content, not readiness, decides whether removal loses work. Git 2.7 supports every command used.
scope: Workspace cleanup, delivery residue removal and status
updates.statement: A registered workspace is removed automatically only when it is clean, has no open Git operation, has advanced from its recorded base, and proves delivered (its tip is an ancestor of the fetched delivery branch) or contained (every non-merge commit outside the delivery branch is patch-equivalent to a delivery commit and no merge outside it has a dense combined diff, or every path it changed since the merge base has its exact content in the delivery branch). Cleanup --all-delivered and the sweep that follows every batch-deliver apply this one predicate to all registered workspaces. Each removal leaves a machine-local retirement record with the outcome and proof. Status lists each registered workspace with the outcome it can prove against the last fetched delivery branch, without fetching.

updates.rationale: Signetum already binds owner authority to exact identities: an approval records actor, date, source and contract digest, and batch-deliver takes the expected base and tip. Binding abandonment to the confirmed tip means a confirmation cannot remove work committed after it. The record keeps the tip so the branch can be recreated while Git retains the objects. batch-discard removed an unpublished batch without any owner authority, which would leave a fourth unproven ending.
updates.statement: maintenance workspace-abandon removes a workspace that proves neither delivered nor contained only when given the exact current tip the owner confirmed, the owner's identity, the confirmation source and a reason; the retirement record keeps them with the tip. It refuses the delivery checkout, open Git operations and staged changes, and discards other uncommitted work only with --discard. It is the only removal for undelivered work; batch-discard is removed.

decisions.reason: The owner directed that every workspace ends in exactly one proven outcome so leftovers stop landing on the owner.

boundaries: Automatic removal never discards uncommitted work or content outside the delivery branch.
revision.summary: Every workspace ends delivered, contained or abandoned, and only a proven outcome removes it.

transaction.reason: Apply the owner-directed workspace outcome rules before implementation
